profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is the Los Angeles Terminal Annex, a large historic post office building at 900 North Alameda Street in downtown Los Angeles, built between 1938 and 1940 and listed as a California Historical Landmark and on the National Register of Historic Places, operated by the United States Postal Service, an independent federal agency. Engineering documentation from DCM Designs, a firm whose project listings reference a data center built at the Terminal Annex, indicates the historic building houses IT infrastructure in addition to its original mail processing and postal functions, consistent with USPS practice of maintaining regional data and network operations within its existing real estate footprint. USPS operates its own nationwide IT infrastructure supporting mail tracking, logistics, retail, and administrative systems, and the Terminal Annex facility is plausibly one node in that network given its downtown Los Angeles location and postal history, but no USPS owned publication describing the Terminal Annex data center capacity, function, or current operational status in detail was found. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
